source.title: FC-Attack: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Auto-Generated Flowcharts
source.authors: Ziyi Zhang; Zhen Sun; Zongmin Zhang; Jihui Guo; Xinlei He

record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful-request compliance in aligned multimodal models using visual and video inputs, a modality-specific extension; it does not test the listed fine-tuning, token-position, compliant-prefill, parameter-localization, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-compliance attack success rates for auto-generated flowcharts and related input conditions. These measure the harmful-request behavior but do not test the specific interventions named by V1–V7. Rows therefore use versions ["none"]. Figure 4 text-only rates are included because the text explicitly describes them. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. It is a multimodal jailbreak (FC-Attack) that puts harmful step descriptions into flowchart images or videos and pairs them with a benign text prompt and a role-play system prompt. Nothing is fine-tuned in the target models (V1, V2). There is no per-token KL or position analysis (V3). The response opening is not prefilled, and suffixes and decoding are not manipulated (V4); decoding is held fixed. No parameters are localized (V5), no cause of shallowness is tested (V6), and no deepening training is done (V7). The only fine-tuned model is the Mistral step generator, and its safety is not measured. The paper does not cite either original source. Its harmful-compliance rates concern modality-specific safety gaps, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that MLLMs are safer in the text modality than in the visual one. They attribute this to insufficient image-modality alignment, shown by entangled benign and attack image embeddings in Appendix D. AdaShield-A cuts average ASR from 58.6% to 1.7% at a cost in MM-Vet utility.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal visual/video jailbreak attack, not the original fine-tuning or token-position method. A separate Mistral-7B-Instruct step-description generator is LoRA-fine-tuned on 5,000 benign activity examples; the target MLLMs receive flowcharts and benign text prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies with the number of flowchart steps, font style, flowchart structure, and input modality. The paper states that decoding settings were held fixed and not varied.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful content delivered as flowchart images with a benign text prompt yields high ASR on several aligned MLLMs. For example, Gemini-1.5 reaches 94% and Qwen2-VL 90%, against 0–6% when the harmful query is given as text only. Adding the generated steps as text gives 0–36%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety alignment of MLLMs generalizes poorly from the text modality to visually delivered harmful content.

fits_no_version.finding: The video version of FC-Attack reaches 86–88% ensemble ASR on three video-capable models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flowchart-based harmful prompts delivered as video elicit harmful outputs from video-capable MLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Flowchart structure (boxes, arrows) and font style change ASR. Claude-3.5 rises from 4% to 28% with the Pacifico font.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visual presentation choices modulate harmful compliance in MLLMs.

record.problems: The study evaluates only 10 representative MLLMs and only English attacks; it says generation parameters were fixed and decoding settings were not investigated. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The tested claim versions are not directly measured.
record.rows_left_out: Not over the 60-row limit. Omitted other font-style entries from Table 3, non-ensemble flowchart-shape entries from Tables 1–2, attack-baseline comparisons in Tables 1 and 4, and defense/benign-utility results in Tables 5–6; these evaluate attack/defense comparisons or utility rather than the specific claim versions. Figure-only values not explicitly described in text were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained target model.
The target MLLMs are not fine-tuned on benign data. The LoRA-tuned Mistral generator's safety is not measured.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding intervention. The attack is input-side, through the visual modality, and decoding parameters were fixed.
No localization or editing of safety-carrying weights or ranks.
No test of why alignment is shallow. Appendix D t-SNE embeddings suggest weaker image-modality alignment, but this is not about token depth or the training objective.
No deepening training. The defenses tested (prompt-based AdaShield, guard models) are not safety-deepening fine-tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The attack uses a system prompt stating no ethical constraints apply, so it combines role-play prompting with visual delivery. The paper does not say whether the text-only controls (r29–r42) used the same system prompt. The abstract's figures (up to 96% for images, 78% for video) do not match Table 4, where the video ensemble reaches 88%. The paper says 'seven' image models in one place and '10 representative MLLMs' elsewhere, which matches 7 image plus 3 video models. All rows are correctly linked to 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: No safety-trained target model is fine-tuned on harmful examples.
The target MLLMs are not fine-tuned on benign instruction data; the separate step-description generator is fine-tuned, but the study does not measure resulting safety changes in that generator.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention; the paper tests visual flowcharts and benign textual prompts.
No weights or ranks carrying safety behavior are localized or edited.
No experiment tests why token-position shallowness occurs.
No training to deepen safety behavior or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.
